statement: statement: Prefix-cylinder patching theorem (charged fan-in-two complete Boolean basis). Let m>p>=1, write inputs as (x,y) with x in {0,1}^p and y in {0,1}^{m-p}. Let g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have a circuit of size s. Let A be a subset of {0,1}^p of cardinality r, and for every a in A let h_a:{0,1}^{m-p}->{0,1} have a circuit of size t_a. Define f(x,y)=g(x,y) XOR (OR_{a in A} ([x=a] AND h_a(y))), with the empty OR equal to 0. Then f has a circuit of size at most s+p+r(p+1)+sum_{a in A} t_a. Proof: If r=0, f=g and the bound holds. Otherwise take disjoint copies of the circuit for g and each h_a, sharing input wires. For each coordinate x_j, form its negation once if needed, using at most p NOT gates. For each a in A, its indicator [x=a] is the conjunction of its p signed input literals, implemented with p-1 binary AND gates. AND this indicator with h_a(y), using one additional AND gate. Thus each gated term costs p gates beyond the shared negations and h_a circuits. OR the r gated terms using r-1 OR gates, then XOR the result with g using one XOR gate. Total: s+sum_a t_a+p+rp+(r-1)+1=s+p+r(p+1)+sum_a t_a. All gates are charged, and all operations are allowed in the basis.

label: S0745
statement: Circuit-description counting lemma (complete fan-in-two Boolean basis). For m input bits and integer s>=0, the number of Boolean functions computable by circuits with at most s gates is at most sum_{r=0}^s 16^r (m+r+2)^{2r+1}. Proof: Count ordered descriptions of circuits with exactly r gates. At gate i (1-based), each of two predecessors has at most m+i+1 choices among the m inputs, two constants, and earlier gates; the gate computes one of 16 binary Boolean functions. The output wire has at most m+r+2 choices. Thus there are at most 16^r (m+r+2)^{2r+1} descriptions. Every such circuit has at least one description, so the number of represented functions is no greater than the number of descriptions. Sum over r<=s. This is an upper bound on the number of easy truth tables, not a circuit lower bound for the MCSP decision function.

structure.gap: This counting lemma does not close the assigned direct lower-bound obligation: it bounds how many truth tables have small circuits, but gives no lower bound on the circuit size needed to decide membership in MCSP[m^c]. The proof-state response was truncated before the open-obligation list, so no specific G-id can be safely attached.

label: S0746
statement: Robust rarity of small-circuit truth tables. Fix m>=1, N=2^m, s>=0, and the model of fan-in-two circuits over all 16 binary Boolean gates, with m free input wires, two constant wires, unrestricted fan-out, and an output wire. Let D(m,s)=sum_{r=0}^s 16^r(m+r+2)^(2r+1). For any integer 0<=t<=N/2, the number of N-bit truth tables at Hamming distance at most t from the truth table of some circuit of size at most s is at most D(m,s) sum_{j=0}^t binom(N,j). Consequently, if D(m,s) sum_{j=0}^t binom(N,j)<2^N, at least one truth table has distance greater than t from every size-s circuit. Proof: For exactly r gates, order gates topologically. At gate i each predecessor wire has at most m+2+(i-1)=m+i+1 choices; its binary gate label has 16 choices. The output has at most m+r+2 choices. Thus at most 16^r (m+r+2)^(2r+1) descriptions exist; summing gives D(m,s), which upper-bounds the number of distinct circuit functions. Around each such truth table, the Hamming ball of radius t has exactly sum_{j=0}^t binom(N,j) strings. The union bound gives the stated count, and strict inequality against 2^N implies an uncovered string. No assumption of disjoint balls is needed. For s=m^c with fixed c and t=floor(delta N), any fixed 0<delta<1/2, the elementary binomial estimate sum_{j<=delta N} binom(N,j)<=2^(N H_2(delta)) gives D times ball <2^N for all sufficiently large m, since log2 D=O(m^c log m)=o(2^m) while 1-H_2(delta)>0. This says many tables are far from easy tables, but does not show the MCSP decision function needs large circuits.

label: S0747
statement: Lemma (minority-support synthesis bound, charged free-literal basis). For every q>=1 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^q->{0,1}, in fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits with free input literals, constants, and unrestricted fan-out, f has a circuit of at most q*min(t,2^q-t) gates, where t=|{x:f(x)=1}|. Proof: Let z=2^q-t. If t=0 or z=0, use a constant output, costing zero. Otherwise choose the smaller of the support and zero-set. For each of its r=min(t,z) assignments, form its q-literal minterm with q-1 AND gates, then OR the r minterms using r-1 gates, for cost r*q-1. If the chosen set is the support, this computes f directly. If it is the zero-set, append one NOT gate, for cost r*q. In either case the cost is at most q*r. This gives a local synthesis bound for every residual truth table; it does not imply restriction stability or accumulation of gate lower bounds.

label: S0748
statement: Corollary (minority support of an MCSP no-instance). Fix q>=1 and the fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit model with free literals, constants, and unrestricted fan-out. If f:{0,1}^q->{0,1} has circuit complexity greater than s, then min(|supp(f)|, 2^q-|supp(f)|) > s/q. Proof: By the minority-support synthesis lemma S0747, C(f) <= q min(|supp(f)|,2^q-|supp(f)|). If the minimum were at most s/q, this upper bound would give C(f)<=s, contradicting C(f)>s. In particular, any residual truth table outside MCSP[s] must disagree with a constant function on more than s/q inputs. This is a necessary condition only; it supplies no lower bound on the number of gates needed to realize the residual map.

structure.evidence: Deduction from the explicitly constructed synthesis bound S0747 by contraposition; no computational premise is used.

statement_start: Lemma (fixed-support/free-coordinate completion bound). Let m>=2, let A and B be disjoint subsets of {0,1}^m with |A|=a and |B|=r, and let h:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support contained in A union B.
statement: Lemma (fixed-support/free-coordinate completion bound). Let m>=2, let A and B be disjoint subsets of {0,1}^m with |A|=a and |B|=r, and let h:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support contained in A union B. In the fan-in-two DAG model with free input wires, free signed input literals, unrestricted fan-out, and AND/OR gates, h has a circuit of at most max(0,(a+r)m-1) gates. Proof. Let T={x:h(x)=1}; then |T|<=a+r. For each x in T, form the minterm M_x by ANDing the m signed input literals specifying x. This uses m-1 binary AND gates per point. If T is nonempty, OR the |T| minterms using |T|-1 binary OR gates. The total is |T|(m-1)+(|T|-1)=|T|m-1 <= (a+r)m-1. If T is empty, use a constant-zero output and zero gates. Thus the bound is max(0,(a+r)m-1). Consequently, fixing every truth-table coordinate outside A union B to zero leaves a residual MCSP[s] predicate identically YES whenever (a+r)m-1<=s (or a+r=0). This restriction-specific degeneracy criterion does not establish stability of the MCSP promise under restrictions or any lower bound.

structure.evidence: For nonempty support, one minterm per supported assignment costs m-1 AND gates, and combining t minterms costs t-1 OR gates, totaling tm-1. Empty support uses a constant-zero output.

statement: Corrected charged-support synthesis lemma. In the fan-in-two basis {AND, OR, NOT}, with every gate charged, constants and input wires free, and unrestricted fan-out, let m≥1 and f:{0,1}^m→{0,1} have support size t. If t=0 or t=2^m, f has a zero-gate constant circuit. Otherwise f has a circuit of size at most min{tm+m−1, (2^m−t)m+m}. Proof: To synthesize f from its t satisfying assignments, compute all m negated input literals once (m NOT gates). For each satisfying assignment, conjoin its m prescribed literals using m−1 AND gates; OR the t minterms using t−1 OR gates. Total: m+t(m−1)+(t−1)=tm+m−1. Alternatively synthesize ¬f from its 2^m−t satisfying assignments and append one NOT gate, for cost m+(2^m−t)(m−1)+(2^m−t−1)+1=(2^m−t)m+m. Taking the smaller construction proves the bound. This corrects the charged-inverter clause, including the m=2 singleton counterexample. It is a synthesis upper bound, not a lower bound for arbitrary circuits or the target MCSP circuit lower bound.

label: S0799
statement:
REPAIR of S0005/S0090: Rigorous linear lower bound for N^{-ε}-MCSP[m^c] promise problem.

DEFINITION (N^{-ε}-MCSP[m^c] promise problem): Fix constants c ≥ 1, ε ∈ (0,1). Let N = 2^m, s = m^c. Basis B2 (16 binary gates, fan-in 2).
- YES instance: the all-zero truth table 0^N (circuit complexity 0 ≤ s).
- NO instances: all tables T ∈ {0,1}^N such that for every circuit C of size ≤ s, dist_H(T, C) > N^{1-ε}.
(Promise: input is either YES or NO.)

LEMMA (Linear lower bound): Any B2 circuit solving N^{-ε}-MCSP[m^c] has size S ≥ N - O(N^{1-ε} + m^{c+1}).

PROOF:
1. Let C be a B2 circuit of size S solving the promise problem. Let R be the set of input bits reachable from the output gate (the read set). The cone of the output has g ≤ S gates and |R| input nodes; it is connected. Each gate has ≤ 2 incoming edges, so total edges ≤ 2g. Connectivity implies |R| + g - 1 ≤ 2g, hence |R| ≤ g + 1 ≤ S + 1.
2. Let U = [N] \ R be unread bits, u = |U| = N - |R|. Let T0 = 0^N (YES). Define random T by T|_R = 0, T|_U ~ Uniform({0,1}^u). Since C does not read U, C(T) = C(T0) = 1 always.
3. Let Y be the set of all truth tables computable by B2 circuits of size ≤ s. Counting: each gate has 16 types and 2 predecessors from N+s nodes. |Circ(N,s)| ≤ Σ_{i=0}^s (16(N+s)^2)^i ≤ (s+1)(16(N+s)^2)^s = 2^{O(s log N)} = 2^{O(m^c · m)} = 2^{O(m^{c+1})}. So M := |Y| ≤ 2^{K m^{c+1}} for some constant K.
4. Fix any g ∈ Y. On U, T is uniform independent of g|_U, so dist_U(T,g) ~ Binomial(u, 1/2). By Hoeffding, for D = u/4: Pr[dist_U(T,g) ≤ D] ≤ exp(-u/8).
5. Union bound: Pr[∃ g ∈ Y : dist(T,g) ≤ D] ≤ M exp(-u/8). If u ≥ 8 ln M and u ≥ 4D (i.e., u ≥ 8 ln M), this probability < 1.
6. Hence there exists a T with C(T)=1 and dist(T,g) > D for all g ∈ Y. For this T to be a valid NO instance we need D ≥ N^{1-ε}. Thus if u ≥ max(4N^{1-ε}, 8 ln M), the circuit errs.
7. Therefore any correct circuit must have u < max(4N^{1-ε}, 8 ln M). So S ≥ |R| - 1 = N - u - 1 > N - 1 - max(4N^{1-ε}, 8K m^{c+1}).
8. This gives S ≥ N - O(N^{1-ε} + m^{c+1}). The union bound exponent is Θ(m^{c+1}), not Θ(m^c log m) as originally claimed.

BARRIER NOTE: The read-set argument fundamentally gives S ≥ |R| - 1 and |R| ≤ N, so it can never yield S = ω(N). Achieving the target S ≥ N(log N)^k requires methods beyond read-set / decision-tree complexity (e.g., gate elimination, communication complexity, or algebraic methods). This lemma repairs the parameter error in S0005/S0090 and precisely locates the linear barrier for this promise problem.

label: S0800
statement: statement: For integers M>=2 and u>=0, if M(1-1/M)^u<1, then a union bound over M bad events each having probability at most (1-1/M)^u proves that the probability of their union is less than 1; equivalently, the strict sufficient threshold is u> ln(M)/[-ln(1-1/M)]. In particular, u> M ln M suffices, while equality at the real-valued threshold does not give the strict contradiction.

structure.evidence: Proof: let E_1,...,E_M be events with P(E_i)<= (1-1/M)^u. By finite subadditivity, P(∪E_i)<=ΣP(E_i)<=M(1-1/M)^u. If this last quantity is <1, the union cannot cover the probability space, so an outcome lies outside every E_i. Since 0<1-1/M<1, taking natural logarithms preserves the equivalence: M(1-1/M)^u<1 iff ln M + u ln(1-1/M)<0 iff u>ln(M)/[-ln(1-1/M)]. Finally -ln(1-x)>=x for 0<x<1, so the denominator is >=1/M and the threshold is <=M ln M; thus u>M ln M suffices. This repairs the invalid equality/boundary inference, but does not by itself establish any MCSP circuit lower bound.

label: S0803
statement: Exact Hamming-ball refinement: Let R be fixed coordinates, U the remaining u coordinates, and Y any family of M Boolean tables. For integer 0<=d<=u, if M sum_{j=0}^d binom(u,j) < 2^u, there is a table T with T|R=0 and dist_H(T,g)>d for every g in Y. Proof: among the 2^u assignments to U, each fixed g has exactly sum_{j=0}^d binom(u,j) assignments within distance d. The union of these M balls therefore contains at most M sum_{j=0}^d binom(u,j) assignments, strictly fewer than 2^u. An assignment outside the union gives T. This is an exact finite-parameter replacement for the tail bound; applying it to the MCSP read-set construction still requires d>=N^(1-epsilon), and the resulting read-set lower bound remains at most linear in N.

label: S0804
statement: statement: Entropy corollary to exact Hamming-ball bound. Let M>=1, u>=1, and integer 0<=d<=u/2. Define H2(p)=-p log2 p-(1-p)log2(1-p), with 0 log2 0=0. If log2(M)<u(1-H2(d/u)), then for any fixed set R of N-u coordinates and any family Y of M Boolean tables, some T with T|R=0 has dist_H(T,g)>d for every g in Y. Proof: Write p=d/u. For p=0, the radius-d ball has size 1. For 0<p<=1/2 and j<=d, p^j(1-p)^(u-j)>=p^d(1-p)^(u-d). Since the binomial probability sum over j=0..d is at most 1, V(u,d)=sum binom(u,j)<=1/(p^d(1-p)^(u-d))=2^(uH2(p)). Thus M V(u,d)<2^u. The M balls cover fewer than all 2^u assignments on the free coordinates, so an uncovered assignment defines T. In the MCSP read-set application this remains limited by the N-coordinate ceiling and requires d>=N^(1-epsilon).

label: S0805
statement: statement: Restriction-aware Hamming-cover lemma: for finite disjoint R,U with |U|=u, fix T|R=0 and finite tables Y. Put h(g)=|{i in R:g_i=1}| and V(u,q)=0 for q<0, sum_{j=0}^q binom(u,j) for 0<=q<u, and 2^u for q>=u. If sum_{g in Y} V(u,d-h(g))<2^u, some completion T|U has distance >d from every g. Proof: a completion within distance d from g must use at most d-h(g) disagreements on U, so its forbidden set has size at most V(u,d-h(g)); the union bound leaves an uncovered completion.

label: S0806
statement: For finite disjoint coordinate sets R,U and a finite family Y of Boolean tables on R∪U, let h(g)=|{i∈R:g_i=1}| and V(u,q)=0 for q<0, V(u,q)=sum_{j=0}^q binom(u,j) for 0≤q<u, and V(u,q)=2^u for q≥u. If sum_{g∈Y} V(u,d-h(g))<2^u, then there exists T with T|R=0 and dist_H(T,g)>d for all g∈Y.

structure.evidence: Proof: For fixed g, the R coordinates already contribute exactly h(g) disagreements since T is fixed to zero on R. Thus any completion on U with total distance at most d must lie within radius d-h(g) of g|U. The number of such completions is V(u,d-h(g)), with the stipulated zero/all-space boundary conventions. The union of these forbidden sets over g∈Y has cardinality at most the sum in the hypothesis, strictly less than the 2^u possible completions of U. Choose any completion outside that union. Its extension T has distance greater than d from every g, as required. This exact lemma supplies the restriction-aware refinement of the ordinary Hamming-cover bound; it does not by itself prove a superlinear MCSP circuit lower bound because the needed weighted sum for the full MCSP circuit family is not established.

label: S0807
statement:
statement: Let f:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be nonconstant and invariant under a transitive group of permutations of its N input coordinates. Every fan-in-two Boolean circuit computing f has at least N−1 nonconstant gates. Consequently, for all sufficiently large m and every fixed c≥1, MCSP[m^c] on N=2^m truth-table bits requires at least N−1 gates in the fan-in-two basis with constants and free fan-out.
proof: For each coordinate i, nonconstancy gives an input x such that changing only coordinate i changes f. Given any coordinate j, transitivity supplies a group element mapping i to j; invariance transports that witness, so changing j can also change f. Thus f depends on all N coordinates. In the output cone of a circuit, let g be its nonconstant gates and k its distinct input variables. The underlying undirected graph on those gates, the k input nodes, and any needed constant source nodes is connected; constants can be treated as additional sources, so more directly, after deleting constants and accounting for constant-valued gate inputs, the output cone connecting k essential input sources to the output has at least k−1 binary gates. Equivalently, each binary gate can combine at most two previously separate dependency components, and starting with k separate input components requires at least k−1 combining gates. Hence g≥N−1. For MCSP[m^c], translation of the Boolean domain permutes the truth-table coordinates and preserves circuit size, so the decision function is invariant under a transitive coordinate action. It is nonconstant for sufficiently large m: the zero table is a YES instance, while a table whose minimum circuit size exceeds m^c is a NO instance, since the number of size-at-most-m^c circuits is at most 2^{O(m^c log m)}<2^{2^m}, whereas there are 2^{2^m} tables. Applying the first assertion proves the stated bound.
scope: Fan-in-two Boolean circuits with constants and free fan-out; truth-table decision MCSP[m^c], N=2^m, sufficiently large m.

label: S0808
statement:
statement: Let f:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be nonconstant and invariant under a transitive group of permutations of its N input coordinates. Any fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit computing f, with free fan-out and constants, has at least N−1 gates. Consequently, for fixed c≥1 and all sufficiently large m, decision MCSP[m^c] on N=2^m truth-table bits requires at least N−1 gates in the model where input negations are free.
proof: Nonconstancy implies that f depends on some coordinate i. For any coordinate j, transitivity gives a permutation in the group taking i to j. Invariance transports a pair of inputs witnessing dependence on i to a pair witnessing dependence on j. Thus the output depends on all N coordinates. In the output cone, retain the N essential input nodes and all gates; include any constant source nodes used. Its underlying undirected graph is connected, has at least N+g vertices if there are g gates, and has at most 2g edges because each gate has at most two incoming wires. A connected graph on at least N+g vertices has at least N+g−1 edges. Hence 2g≥N+g−1 and g≥N−1. For MCSP[m^c] with free input negations, translating the truth-table index by x↦x⊕a permutes table coordinates and preserves circuit size, so the decision function is invariant under a transitive coordinate action. It is nonconstant for sufficiently large m: the zero table is a yes instance, while counting size-at-most-m^c circuits gives at most 2^{O(m^c log(m+m^c))} tables, fewer than 2^{2^m}. The general lemma then gives the stated bound.
scope: The MCSP consequence assumes free input negations. With counted NOT gates, this symmetry argument does not establish the consequence because translation may increase circuit size.

label: S0809
statement:
statement: Let C be a finite fan-in-two Boolean DAG circuit and rho a partial assignment to its input variables. If t gates of C compute constant Boolean functions after restriction by rho, then C|rho has a fan-in-two circuit with at most |C|-t gates.
proof: Process the circuit gates in topological order. For each gate whose restricted Boolean function is constant, replace its output wire by that constant and delete the gate. For any other gate, retain it, feeding it the already restricted outputs of its predecessors; its resulting function is precisely its cofactor under rho. The output wire therefore computes C|rho. Exactly the t specified gates have been deleted, so the resulting circuit has at most |C|-t gates. Fan-in remains at most two and the DAG order is preserved.
scope: All finite fan-in-two Boolean DAG circuits, with arbitrary fan-out, and all partial assignments rho. The result only applies when t gates are known to become constant; it gives no lower bound on t for MCSP restrictions.

label: S0811
statement: statement: For every Boolean function f depending essentially on k input variables, every fan-in-two Boolean circuit computing f has at least k-1 gates in its output cone, even with free fan-out and constant sources. Proof: retain the output cone and the k essential input vertices. Each essential input has a directed path to the output, so the underlying undirected graph on these input vertices and the gates on their paths is connected. If it has g gate vertices, it has at least k+g-1 distinct edges. Every such edge is incident to a gate and each gate has at most two incoming wires, so there are at most 2g edges. Thus k+g-1 <= 2g and g >= k-1.

label: S0813
statement: statement: Let C_m(f) be the minimum number of fan-in-two Boolean gates computing f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, allowing all 16 binary Boolean operations, constants, and free fan-out. For a in {0,1}^m define f_a(x)=f(x xor a). Then |C_m(f_a)-C_m(f)|<=|a|<=m. Proof: given a circuit for f, replace each input x_i with x_i xor a_i. For each i with a_i=1, form NOT(x_i) using one binary gate, e.g. x_i NAND x_i, and feed that value wherever x_i was used. This adds at most |a| gates and computes f_a. Hence C_m(f_a)<=C_m(f)+|a|. Since (f_a)_a=f, applying the same construction in reverse gives C_m(f)<=C_m(f_a)+|a|, proving the absolute-difference bound. Thus translations are exact symmetries of truth-table coordinates but only additive-m recodings in this gate-count convention; they preserve an MCSP threshold exactly only when the recoding overhead is accounted for.

label: S0816
statement: statement: For integers m>=1 and d>=1, let F:{0,1}^m->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size s. If G differs from F on at most d inputs, then G has such a circuit of size at most s+md+m+3. Proof: Let A be the set of changed inputs, |A|=e<=d. Share at most m NOT gates to form negated input literals. For each a in A, its equality indicator E_a is the conjunction of the m literals specifying a, using m-1 AND gates. OR the e indicators using e-1 OR gates (if e=1 this costs 0). Their disjunction P is exactly the indicator of A. Then G=F XOR P. An AND/OR/NOT circuit computes XOR with at most four gates: compute F OR P, F AND P, negate the latter, and AND the first with that negation. Thus the added size is at most m+e(m-1)+(e-1)+4=em+m+3<=dm+m+3. If e=0, G=F and the bound holds directly.

statement:
statement: Support-size bound for fan-in-at-most-two circuits. Let C be a Boolean circuit with arbitrary depth, free fan-out, constants, and g gates. If its output depends on k distinct input variables, then g >= k-1.
proof: Take the output cone, retain its k essential input vertices and its g' gate vertices, where g'<=g. The underlying undirected graph is connected because every retained vertex has a path to the output. It therefore has at least k+g'-1 edges. Each gate has at most two incoming wires, so the graph has at most 2g' edges. Hence k+g'-1<=2g', so g'>=k-1 and g>=k-1. Constant inputs may be omitted: they are not needed to connect essential inputs to the output.
scope: All finite fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits with free fan-out and constants, with no depth restriction.

label: S0843
statement: statement: For m,s≥1, N=2^m, and fan-in-two Boolean circuits over AND, OR, NOT, and constants with free fan-out, the number of m-input Boolean functions computable with at most s gates is at most (s+1)16^s(N+s)^(2s+1). Proof: For each exact size j≤s, encode gates in topological order. Each gate has at most 16 choices of type and two predecessor wires, each selected among at most N+s wires; the output wire has at most N+s choices. Thus there are at most 16^j(N+s)^(2j+1) encodings. Summing the s+1 size classes and bounding each term by 16^s(N+s)^(2s+1) gives the result. Every represented function has at least one encoding, so the function count is no larger. Therefore the fraction of truth tables accepted by MCSP[s] is at most (s+1)16^s(N+s)^(2s+1)/2^N; for fixed c and s=m^c this tends to zero as m grows.

statement: statement: Repair lemma: Let F:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be invariant under every XOR translation x↦x⊕a. If F is nonconstant, then every input coordinate is essential. Proof: If coordinate i is inessential, for any j choose a=e_i⊕e_j (and for j=i use a=0). Translation invariance gives F(x)=F(x⊕a). Inessentiality of i applied at x⊕a gives F(x⊕a)=F((x⊕a)⊕e_i)=F(x⊕e_j). Hence F is insensitive to j. This holds for every j, so F is constant, contradiction. Consequently any fan-in-at-most-two circuit with free fan-out computing F has at least N−1 gates: the output cone is connected, contains all N essential input vertices and g gate vertices, has at least N+g−1 distinct edges and at most 2g incoming wires, hence N−1≤g.

statement: For every integer m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with exactly t>=1 satisfying inputs, f has a fan-in-two circuit over AND, OR, NOT, constants, with free input negations, of size at most tm-1. statement: For every m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with t ones, in the fan-in-two AND/OR basis with free input negations, its circuit size is at most 0 if q=0 and at most mq-1 if q=min(t,2^m-t)>=1. Proof: If t<=2^(m-1), disjoin the t minterms for the one-set, costing t(m-1)+(t-1)=mt-1 gates. Each width-m clause costs m-1 OR gates, and conjunction of q clauses costs q-1 AND gates, giving mq-1 gates for f. Thus for either smaller support, a DNF (one-set) or CNF (zero-set) costs mq-1. If q=0, f is constant.

statement: statement: Cofactor lemma. Let m>=1, f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, and f_b be the (m-1)-variable cofactor obtained by fixing the last input to b, for b in {0,1}. In fan-in-at-most-two circuits over AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1 with free fan-out and gate-count size, C(f_b)<=C(f) for each b, and C(f)<=C(f_0)+C(f_1)+4. Proof: Substitute the constant b for the last input in a minimum circuit for f; this computes f_b without adding gates, so C(f_b)<=C(f). For the upper bound, take circuits for f_0 and f_1 and combine their outputs as f=(NOT x_m AND f_0) OR (x_m AND f_1). This uses one NOT and three binary gates, hence four additional gates. Exact scope: every m>=1 and the stated basis and size convention.

statement: statement: Shannon cofactor construction (corrected verification indexing). For m>=1, write an input as (y,b) with y in {0,1}^{m-1} and b in {0,1}; define f_b(y)=f(y,b). For fan-in-at-most-two circuits over AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1 with free fan-out and gate-count size, C(f_b)<=C(f), and C(f)<=C(f_0)+C(f_1)+4. Proof: Substitute the constant b for the last input in a minimum circuit for f, preserving all gates and possibly simplifying, so C(f_b)<=C(f). Conversely, given circuits for f_0 and f_1, compute (NOT b AND f_0(y)) OR (b AND f_1(y)); this uses one NOT and three binary gates, computes f(y,b) for both b values, and yields the bound. label: S0855
statement:
statement: For integers m>=1 and s>=0, let F_{m,s} be the Boolean functions on {0,1}^m computable by fan-in-at-most-two circuits over AND, OR, NOT and constants, with free fan-out, and count each gate once. Then |F_{m,s}| <= (s+1)(m+s+2)[3(m+s+2)^2]^s. Consequently the fraction of length-N truth tables accepted by MCSP[s], N=2^m, is at most this quantity divided by 2^N.
proof: For each g<=s, topologically order the g gates. Each gate has at most 3 choices of type and at most (m+g+2)^2 ordered choices of sources (m primary inputs, two constants, and at most g gate outputs). This overcounts by permitting later gates and invalid cycles, and by giving NOT gates two sources. The output selector has at most m+g+2 choices. Thus the number of descriptions with g gates is at most (m+g+2)[3(m+g+2)^2]^g. Summing over g=0,...,s and upper-bounding each factor by its value at s gives at most (s+1)(m+s+2)[3(m+s+2)^2]^s descriptions. Every function in F_{m,s} has a description, so |F_{m,s}| is at most this count. There are 2^(2^m) functions on m bits, proving the density consequence.
scope: All m>=1 and integer s>=0; fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits, free fan-out, constants, output selected from input/constant/gate. This bounds the density of accepted truth tables only and does not lower-bound the circuit complexity of the MCSP decision function.

statement:
statement: Transitive-symmetry essentiality lemma. Let G act transitively on the coordinates of {0,1}^N by coordinate permutations. If F:{0,1}^N->{0,1} satisfies F(x)=F(gx) for every g in G and is nonconstant, then every coordinate of F is essential. Proof: If coordinate i is inessential, then for any coordinate j, transitivity gives g with g(i)=j. For any x, invariance gives F(x)=F(g^{-1}x); the vectors x and g^{-1}x differ only at coordinate i when x is replaced by x xor e_j? More directly, invariance transports insensitivity: F(x)=F(x xor e_j) follows by applying invariance to x and x xor e_j after choosing g with g(i)=j, since g^{-1} sends e_j to e_i. Thus F is insensitive to every coordinate, hence constant, contradiction. Therefore all N coordinates are essential. In the fan-in-at-most-two circuit model with free fan-out, this implies at least N-1 gates by the connected-output-cone edge count: with k=N essential input vertices and g' gate vertices in the output cone, connectivity requires at least N+g'-1 distinct edges, while at most 2g' wires enter gates; hence g'>=N-1.
scope: All finite N, all transitive permutation groups G on the N input coordinates, and all G-invariant nonconstant Boolean functions; circuit consequence in fan-in-at-most-two circuits with free fan-out and constants.
limitation: The lemma applies to an MCSP truth-table decision function only after proving invariance under a transitive group of truth-table-position permutations and nonconstancy for the chosen threshold. The resulting N-1 bound is linear and does not prove the assigned N(log N)^k target.

statement:
statement: Let N>=1, let G be a transitive group of coordinate permutations of {0,1}^N, and let F:{0,1}^N->{0,1} satisfy F(gx)=F(x) for all g,x. If F is nonconstant, every coordinate is essential. Proof: Suppose coordinate i is inessential, so F(y)=F(y xor e_i) for every y. Fix j and choose g in G with g(i)=j. Then g^{-1}e_j=e_i. For arbitrary x, invariance gives F(x)=F(g^{-1}x), and F(x xor e_j)=F(g^{-1}(x xor e_j))=F(g^{-1}x xor e_i)=F(g^{-1}x), using inessentiality of i. Thus F is insensitive to every coordinate and hence constant, contradiction. Circuit corollary: in a fan-in-at-most-two circuit with free fan-out and constants, the output cone contains all N essential inputs and g' gate vertices. Its underlying graph is connected, so has at least N+g'-1 distinct edges; at most 2g' wires enter gates. Thus g'>=N-1.
scope: All finite N>=1 and transitive coordinate-permutation groups; circuit corollary for fan-in-at-most-two circuits with free fan-out and constants.
limitation: This proves only an N-1 gate lower bound. It does not establish the assigned N(log N)^k lower bound for MCSP[m^c].

statement:
statement: Cofactor reconstruction with constant and equal branches. Let f:{0,1}^m→{0,1}, and let f_0,f_1 be its cofactors at coordinate i. In the fan-in-at-most-two basis {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1} with free fan-out, C(f)≤C(f_0)+C(f_1)+4; if f_0 is constant 0, then C(f)≤C(f_1)+1, if f_0 is constant 1, then C(f)≤C(f_1)+2, and if f_0=f_1, then C(f)≤C(f_0). Proof: In general compute (¬x_i∧f_0)∨(x_i∧f_1), using at most four gates (one NOT, two AND, one OR). If f_0=0, use x_i∧f_1; if f_0=1, use ¬x_i∨f_1; if f_0=f_1, output the shared cofactor circuit directly, since the function is independent of x_i. The symmetric cases follow by swapping the branch labels and using ¬x_i where needed.
scope: Every m≥1, every Boolean function and coordinate, with minimum circuit size over fan-in-at-most-two AND/OR/NOT/constants and free fan-out.
limitation: This is a local reconstruction inequality only. It gives no lower bound on MCSP[m^c] circuit size without an additional argument showing many restricted subproblems have suitably expensive and distinct cofactors.

statement:
statement: For f(x,y)=not x OR y, the x=0 cofactor is constant 1 and the x=1 cofactor is y; the function is computable in two gates but not in at most one gate in the fan-in-at-most-two AND/OR/NOT basis with constants and free input wires.
scope: The two-input function and the stated circuit basis only.
proof: Truth table in lexicographic input order is (1,1,0,1). A zero-gate output is an input wire or constant, none of which has this truth table. A one-gate output is NOT of an input, or AND/OR of two input wires/constants. Direct enumeration of these possibilities gives no target truth table. The construction NOT x followed by OR with y uses two gates.
limitation: This finite counterexample refutes only the proposed one-extra-gate reconstruction claim; it does not address the general MCSP lower-bound obligation.

label: S0860
statement: statement: Sparse-table constructive MCSP lemma. For every integer m>=1, put N=2^m and let f be a Boolean function on m input bits with t satisfying inputs. In the fan-in-two basis {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1}, with free fan-out and size counting gates, if t>=1 then C(f)<=tm-1; if t=0 then C(f)=0. Consequently for every integer s>=0, every truth table with at most floor((s+1)/m) ones is a yes-instance of MCSP[s]. Proof: For each satisfying input a in {0,1}^m construct the minterm M_a as the AND of the m input literals that agree with a, using a binary AND tree of m-1 gates (for m=1 this uses zero gates). OR the t minterms using t-1 binary OR gates (zero if t=1). At input x, M_a(x)=1 exactly when x=a, so the OR is 1 exactly on the support of f and computes f. The total is t(m-1)+(t-1)=tm-1. For t=0 the constant-zero circuit has zero gates. If t<=floor((s+1)/m), then tm-1<=s, proving the consequence.

label: S0861
statement: statement: Nonconstancy and linear decision-circuit lower bound for polynomial-threshold MCSP. Fix an integer c>=1. For all sufficiently large m, let N=2^m and s=m^c, and define h_m:{0,1}^N->{0,1} by h_m(T)=1 iff the truth table T is computed by a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit over AND, OR, NOT, constants, with free fan-out and at most s gates. Then h_m is nonconstant, every one of its N input coordinates is essential, and every fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing h_m has at least N-1 gates. Proof: The constant-zero function has a zero-gate circuit, so h_m(0^N)=1. A topologically ordered circuit with j gates has at most 5^j(m+j)^(2j) descriptions: each gate has at most five types, and at most two predecessor wires chosen from the m inputs and earlier gates. Summing over j=0..s gives at most (s+1)5^s(m+s)^(2s) descriptions. For fixed c and s=m^c, the base-2 logarithm of this bound is O(m^c log m), which is less than 2^m for all sufficiently large m. There are 2^(2^m) truth tables, so some table is not computed by any such circuit; h_m is nonconstant. For a in {0,1}^m, translating table indices by x -> x xor a preserves circuit size, by relabeling each input wire accordingly; the inverse translation is the same operation. Thus h_m is invariant under every such translation. These translations act transitively on the N table positions. If h_m were insensitive to one coordinate, translation invariance would make it insensitive to every coordinate, forcing it to be constant, a contradiction. Hence all N coordinates are essential. In a fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing a function depending on all N inputs, its output cone is connected and contains the N essential input vertices and g gate vertices. It has at least N+g-1 distinct undirected edges, while its gates contribute at most 2g incoming wires. Therefore g>=N-1. Scope: fixed c>=1 and all sufficiently large m, for the stated basis and gate-count convention. This gives only a linear lower bound for MCSP[m^c], not the target N(log N)^k bound.

statement: statement: Corrected description-count nonconstancy lemma for MCSP. Fix c>=1, let N=2^m and s=m^c, and define h_m(T)=1 iff T is computed by a fan-in-at-most-two circuit with j<=s gates over {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1}, with m input variables and free fan-out. For all sufficiently large m, h_m is nonconstant. Proof: For each j, encode a circuit by a topological list of j gates, a type per gate, at most two predecessor indices per gate chosen from the m inputs and j earlier gate positions, and a designated output wire among the m+j wires. This gives at most 5^j(m+j)^(2j+1) descriptions; unused predecessor slots in a unary or constant gate are allowed as overcounting. Summing j=0..s gives at most (s+1)5^s(m+s)^(2s+1) descriptions. Its base-2 logarithm is O(s log(m+s))=O(m^c log m), which is less than N=2^m for sufficiently large m. Hence fewer than 2^N truth tables are computed by size-s circuits. The zero table is computed by a constant-zero circuit, so h_m takes both values. Scope: fixed c, sufficiently large m, exact stated basis and gate-count convention.

statement: Lemma: Let N=2^m and H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be invariant under input-assignment translations P_a, where (P_aT)_x=T_{x xor a}. If H is nonconstant, it depends on every table coordinate. Proof: Suppose H omits coordinate x. For any y, choose a=x xor y. If T,T' differ only at y, then P_aT and P_aT' differ only at x. Thus H(P_aT)=H(P_aT'); translation invariance gives H(T)=H(T'), so H omits y. This holds for all y, contradicting nonconstancy. A fan-in-at-most-two circuit with free fan-out computing H therefore has at least N-1 gates: its output cone is connected, contains the N essential input vertices and g gate vertices, has at least N+g-1 edges and at most 2g incoming wires, so g>=N-1. MCSP_s is invariant under input-assignment translations because x->x xor a is a circuit-size-preserving input renaming. Combined with S0862, this gives only a linear bound, not the target superlinear bound.

A fan-in-at-most-two circuit with free fan-out computing H therefore has at least N-1 gates: its output cone is connected, contains the N essential input vertices and g gate vertices, has at least N+g-1 edges and at most 2g incoming wires, so g>=N-1. MCSP_s is invariant under input-assignment translations because x->x xor a is a circuit-size-preserving input renaming. Combined with S0862, this gives only a linear bound, not the target superlinear bound.

statement: For every m>=1, every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, every coordinate i, and every integer d with 0<=d<=m, let f|rho range over the 2^d cofactors obtained by fixing the first d coordinates in any fixed ordering beginning with i. In the fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT/constant circuit model with free fan-out, C(f) <= sum_rho C(f|rho) + 4(2^d-1). Proof: for d=0 equality holds. For d>=1, partition the restrictions by the last fixed bit. For each restriction rho to the first d-1 coordinates, f|rho is reconstructed from its two next cofactors h0,h1 by (NOT x) AND h0 OR x AND h1, using two AND gates and one OR gate, with NOT x either shared globally or counted once. Thus C(f|rho) <= C(h0)+C(h1)+4. Summing over the 2^(d-1) prefixes gives sum_{|rho|=d-1} C(f|rho) <= sum_{|rho|=d} C(f|rho)+4*2^(d-1). Iterating yields C(f) <= sum_{|rho|=d} C(f|rho)+4 sum_{j=0}^{d-1}2^j = sum C(f|rho)+4(2^d-1).
scope: All Boolean functions on m variables, fixed ordering of d distinct variables, fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT/constant circuits with free fan-out; size counts gates and allows sharing. This is an upper bound on parent complexity from leaf cofactor complexities; it gives no superlinear MCSP decision-circuit lower bound.
proof: Induction by restriction depth. At each internal node, Shannon expansion f=(¬x∧f0)∨(x∧f1) uses two binary AND gates and one binary OR gate plus at most one NOT gate, so parent complexity is at most the sum of child complexities plus 4. Sum this inequality over all nodes at a level and iterate for d levels. The geometric sum of level costs is 4(1+2+...+2^(d-1))=4(2^d-1).

label: S0865
statement: statement: Restriction-composition lemma for fan-in-two Boolean circuits. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, m>=1, and let f_0,f_1 be its cofactors at the last input. In the basis {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1} with free fan-out, if C(f)<=s, then C(f_b)<=s for b in {0,1}. Conversely, if C(f_0)<=s_0 and C(f_1)<=s_1, then C(f)<=s_0+s_1+3. Proof: For the first implication, substitute constant b for the last input in a circuit for f; this preserves its gate count and computes f_b. For the converse, take circuits for f_0 and f_1 on the first m-1 inputs, and combine their outputs with a selector: f=(NOT x_m AND f_0) OR (x_m AND f_1). Two AND gates, one OR gate, and one NOT gate suffice, so the total is s_0+s_1+4 if NOT x_m is not free. With free input negations, the total is s_0+s_1+3. Scope: circuits over the stated basis with free input negations; constants are allowed. Therefore if both cofactors have size at most s, then C(f)<=2s+3.

label: S0866
statement: statement: Cofactor composition, with gate conventions explicit. Let m>=1 and f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}; let f_0,f_1 be the cofactors on the first m-1 variables after fixing x_m=0,1. label: S0867
statement: statement: Sparse-support upper bound (explicit basis). For every m>=1 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, let t=|f^{-1}(1)| and q=min(t,2^m-t). In fan-in-two AND/OR circuits with free input negations, constants, and free fan-out, C(f)=0 when q=0 and C(f)<=m q-1 when q>=1. Proof: If t<=2^{m-1}, for each satisfying assignment a form its minterm M_a, a conjunction of m literals, using m-1 binary AND gates; OR the t minterms using t-1 OR gates. This computes f at cost t(m-1)+(t-1)=mt-1=mq-1. If t>2^{m-1}, let Z=f^{-1}(0). For each z in Z form the clause that is false exactly on z, namely the disjunction of the m literals each opposite to z's bit; it costs m-1 OR gates. AND the q such clauses using q-1 gates. This computes f and costs q(m-1)+(q-1)=mq-1. If q=0, f is constant. The statement concerns an explicit representation upper bound only; it gives no lower bound on the MCSP decision function and does not close the superlinear target.

label: S0868
statement: For m>=2 and 0<=s<m-1, every truth-table coordinate is essential for MCSP_s in the fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT/constants model, with NOT counted and free fan-out. Proof: For any position a, the zero table has circuit size 0, while the singleton table e_a represents a function depending on all m variables. Any circuit whose output depends on k variables has at least k-1 gates: its output cone is connected, has at least k+g-1 edges for g gates, and at most 2g incoming wires. Thus C(e_a)>=m-1>s. The two tables differ only at a, so MCSP_s changes at that coordinate. This holds for every a.

label: S0870
statement: statement: Lemma (circuit description count). Fix m>=1 and the fan-in-at-most-two basis with gates AND, OR, NOT, constants 0,1, free fan-out, and an output that may be an input, constant, or gate. For integer s>=0, the number of functions {0,1}^m->{0,1} computed by circuits with at most s gates is at most B(m,s)=sum_{g=0}^s (m+g+2)[3(m+g+2)^2]^g. Consequently, if B(m,s)<2^(2^m), some m-bit Boolean function has circuit size greater than s.

structure.evidence: Proof: Topologically order the g gates. For each gate i, its type has at most 3 choices. Each of its at most two ordered inputs can be chosen from the m primary inputs, two constants, and at most g earlier gates, so the number of ordered source pairs is at most (m+g+2)^2; this also overcounts unary NOT gates. The output has at most m+g+2 choices. Thus circuits with exactly g gates have at most (m+g+2)[3(m+g+2)^2]^g encodings. Summing over g=0,...,s upper-bounds all size-at-most-s circuits; distinct encodings may compute the same function, so it is also an upper bound on distinct functions. There are exactly 2^(2^m) m-bit Boolean functions. Strict inequality leaves at least one function uncomputed by every size-at-most-s circuit. Scope is exactly the stated basis/model. This is a hard-function counting result, not a lower bound for MCSP's decision predicate.

label: S0871
statement: statement: Lemma (within-layer essentiality). Fix m>=1, s>=0, and let F_s:{0,1}^{2^m}->{0,1} be the MCSP predicate for fan-in-at-most-two circuits over AND, OR, NOT, constants, with free fan-out. For truth-table positions u,v in {0,1}^m with equal Hamming weight, the coordinate u is essential for F_s if and only if coordinate v is essential. Proof: Since |u|=|v|, some permutation pi of the m input coordinates maps u to v. For a truth table z, define (pi z)(x)=z(pi^{-1}x). Relabeling every primary input of a circuit by pi^{-1} gives a circuit for pi z of identical gate count; applying the inverse relabeling gives C(pi z)=C(z). Hence F_s(pi z)=F_s(z) for every z. If coordinate u is inessential, then F_s(z)=F_s(z with bit u flipped) for every z. Applying invariance under pi and pi^{-1} shows F_s(z)=F_s(z with bit v flipped) for every z, so v is inessential. The reverse implication follows by using pi^{-1}. Scope: exact for all m,s in the stated basis/model. Limitation: permutations preserve Hamming weight of positions and give no conclusion between distinct layers; this does not prove a superlinear circuit lower bound for F_s.

statement: statement: Let m>=1, let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have a fan-in-two Boolean circuit over {AND, OR, NOT, 0, 1} of size C(f), with free fan-out, and let T be any subset of {0,1}^m of size t. Then C(f XOR 1_T) <= C(f) when t=0, and C(f XOR 1_T) <= C(f)+mt+m+3 when t>=1. Proof: For t>=1, construct h=1_T as the OR of the t minterms for elements of T. Use at most m NOT gates to form all negative literals, t(m-1) AND gates for the minterms, and t-1 OR gates to combine them, so h costs at most mt+m-1 gates. Given output wires f and h, compute f XOR h as (f OR h) AND NOT(f AND h), using four gates: one OR, one AND, one NOT, one AND. Thus the added cost is at most mt+m+3. For t=0, 1_T is identically zero and f XOR 0=f. The construction includes m=1 and t=2^m. This is an upper bound for changing t truth-table entries, not a lower bound on the MCSP decision function.

statement:
statement: Lemma (Essential variables of MCSP decision): For all sufficiently large m and any fixed c >= 1, let s = m^c and let F_s: {0,1}^{2^m} -> {0,1} be the MCSP decision function (F_s(TT) = 1 iff the Boolean function with truth table TT has fan-in-2 circuit size <= s). Then every one of the 2^m input variables of F_s is essential. That is, for every index i in {0,1}^m, there exist truth tables f, g differing only at position i such that F_s(f) = 1 and F_s(g) = 0.

Proof: 
1. (Existence of an easy function with a hard neighbor at some position) By the standard gate-counting bound (S0005), |F_s| <= (s+1)(N+s+1)(8(N+s)^2)^s where N = 2^m. This is at most 2^{O(s log N)} = 2^{O(m^{c+1})}. For sufficiently large m, 2^{O(m^{c+1})} < 2^N / (N+1) because 2^N = 2^{2^m} grows doubly-exponentially in m while the bound is singly-exponential. If every f in F_s had all N neighbors also in F_s, then the union of radius-1 Hamming balls around F_s would be contained in F_s, implying |F_s| * (N+1) >= 2^N (since every function is either in F_s or at distance >= 2 from F_s, but the complement has size 2^N - |F_s| > 0). This contradicts |F_s| < 2^N/(N+1). Hence there exists some f_0 in F_s and some i_0 in {0,1}^m such that flipping bit i_0 yields g_0 not in F_s.

2. (Symmetry under input permutations) For any permutation pi in S_m of the m input variables, define the action on truth tables by (pi * TT)(x) = TT(pi^{-1}(x)). If a function f has a circuit C of size <= s, then f o pi has a circuit of the same size (obtained by permuting the input wires of C according to pi). Thus C(f o pi) = C(f), so F_s(pi * TT) = F_s(TT). The action of S_m on {0,1}^m is transitive: for any i, j in {0,1}^m there exists pi with pi(i_0) = j.

3. (All positions are essential) For any target position j, choose pi with pi(i_0) = j. Let f = pi * f_0 and g = pi * g_0. Then f and g differ only at position j (since f_0 and g_0 differ only at i_0). We have F_s(f) = F_s(f_0) = 1 and F_s(g) = F_s(g_0) = 0. Thus bit j is essential for F_s. Since j was arbitrary, all 2^m variables are essential.

Scope: All m >= m_0(c), all c >= 1, fan-in-2 circuits with free fan-out and constants. The lemma is a structural property of the MCSP decision function itself, not of the functions in F_s.

statement: statement: Correction-cost lemma. Let m>=1, let g:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size s with free fan-out, and let h differ from g on a set D of r truth-table positions. Then h has such a circuit of size at most s+rm+m+4. Proof: Let P be the indicator of D. For each a in D take its width-m minterm. The OR of these r minterms costs r(m-1)+(r-1)=rm-1 binary AND/OR gates when r>=1; all needed negated input literals are shared using at most m NOT gates. (For r=0, P=0.) Compute h=g XOR P using (g AND NOT P) OR (NOT g AND P), with at most five gates including the two NOT gates. Thus for r>=1 the total added size is at most rm-1+m+5 <= rm+m+4; for r=0 no added gates are needed. This lemma bounds the circuit cost of correcting a bounded number of truth-table entries, but does not lower-bound the MCSP decision function.

statement: statement: Bounded truth-table correction lemma. Let m>=1, N=2^m, and let g,h:{0,1}^m->{0,1} differ on at most r positions. In the fan-in-two AND/OR basis with free input negations, the circuit size of h is at most the circuit size of g plus rm+m+4. Proof: Let D be the disagreement set, of size d<=r. Compute P as the OR of the d minterms indexed by D; for d>=1 this uses d(m-1)+(d-1)=dm-1 AND/OR gates, and all negated input literals are available under the free-negation convention. For d=0 use P=0. Then h=g XOR P. Implement XOR with (g AND NOT P) OR (NOT g AND P), using at most five binary AND/OR/NOT gates beyond the circuits for g and P. For d>=1 the added cost is at most dm-1+5<=rm+4<=rm+m+4; for d=0 the added cost is zero. Scope: every m>=1, every pair g,h and every r>=0, with fan-out free, constants available, and input negations uncharged. The exhaustive check cm-d19355457ab54cd2 found no violations for all truth tables through m=4 and all flip sets of size at most two; it is finite evidence only.

structure.evidence: The proof constructs the disagreement indicator exactly as a minterm DNF and combines it with g by XOR. The construction is exact for every truth-table pair; cm-d19355457ab54cd2 independently checked the support-based count on its stated finite range, but is not needed for the proof.

statement: Let X,Y be finite sets, φ:X→Y, and f:Y→{0,1}. Then |{x∈X:f(φ(x))=1}| = Σ_{y∈Y}|φ⁻¹(y)|f(y). Thus bijective substitutions preserve the accepting count and fraction. If φ(x)=Ax+b is an affine map F₂ᵏ→F₂ᵏ of rank r, the substituted accepting count is 2^(k−r)|{y∈im(φ):f(y)=1}|.
proof: Partition X into the disjoint fibers φ⁻¹(y), for y∈Y. The accepting inputs are the disjoint union of φ⁻¹(y) over those y for which f(y)=1, so their count is the sum of the fiber sizes shown. For a bijection every fiber has size one, and |X|=|Y|, giving preservation of both count and fraction. For φ(x)=Ax+b with rank(A)=r, each y in the image has a nonempty fiber that is a coset of ker(A), hence has size 2^(k−r); points outside the image have empty fibers. Substitution in the sum gives the affine-map formula.

statement:
statement: Let k>=1, let phi(x)=Ax+b be an affine bijection F_2^k -> F_2^k, and let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size s over {AND, OR, NOT}. Then f∘phi has the same number and fraction of accepting inputs as f, and has a circuit of size at most s+4k(k-1)+k. This bound applies to the specified affine substitution; it makes no claim about arbitrary bijections or a decrease in the W-C potential.
proof: Since phi is a bijection, it permutes the 2^k inputs. Thus x↦f(phi(x)) accepts exactly the preimages under phi of f's accepting inputs, so its accepting count and density equal f's. To implement phi, compute each coordinate (Ax+b)_i as the XOR of the variables whose coefficients in row i of A are 1, optionally complemented when b_i=1. A parity of t variables uses t-1 two-input XOR gates when t>=1; the empty parity is a constant. Implement each XOR with four gates over {AND, OR, NOT}, using (u OR v) AND NOT(u AND v). Across k output coordinates this uses at most 4k(k-1) gates; complementing coordinates costs at most k NOT gates. Feed these k outputs into the original circuit for f, adding its s gates. The total is at most s+4k(k-1)+k. Invertibility is used for density preservation; the circuit-size upper bound itself does not require it.

statement: Let k>=1, A in F_2^{k x k} have rank r, b in F_2^k, phi(x)=Ax+b, and f:F_2^k->{0,1}. Then |{x in F_2^k:f(phi(x))=1}| = 2^(k-r)|{y in b+im(A):f(y)=1}|. Proof: The image of phi is b+im(A). Partition the accepting x by y=phi(x) and sum the fiber sizes over accepting y to obtain the identity.

statement: STAGE 2 LEMMA (space ceiling; Lemma FB2 of research/PNP-001/lab/feedback-complexity/FEEDBACK-NOTE-2026-11-20.md, proof written out there): for MCSP[s] (and search-MCSP[s]) on truth tables of length N = 2^n read in one pass, there is a one-pass algorithm with O(s log(n+s)) = O(s log s) bits of memory (s >= n): keep the lexicographically first size-<=s circuit consistent with the prefix read so far; on a disagreeing bit search the next consistent circuit (unbounded update time). Hence every pure space / communication argument ends at this value, which lies inside poly(s): only an UPDATE-TIME lower bound can establish the Stage 1 target.

statement: LEMMA (affine updates, F_2 or any finite field): a one-pass total algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] (N = 2^n, SC_s nonempty) whose update z_{t+1} = M_t z_t + u_t b + c_t is affine in (state, bit) must use S >= N state bits. Proof: the state map p -> z(p) on {0,1}^t is affine, so its fibres are cosets of kernels of dimension >= t - S, hence of size >= 2 when t > S. A live prefix p (a prefix of some T in SC_s) has a second prefix p' in its fibre. By Satz B (S0010), p' is neither live nor dead-sharing, a contradiction, so S+1 > N. label: S0024
statement: LEMMA L-F3 (repair of S0021 for p=3, linear and affine). Let A in F_3^{k x t}, c in F_3^k, and let phi(p) = A p + c on {0,1}^t. Then phi is injective on {0,1}^t iff rank_{F_3}(A) = t. PROOF. (a) If rank A < t, pick v != 0 with Av = 0. Each entry v_i lies in {0,1,2} = {0,1,-1} mod 3; let v' in {-1,0,1}^t be its representative, v' = p - q with p = max(v',0), q = max(-v',0) in {0,1}^t, p != q. Then phi(p) - phi(q) = A(p-q) = Av' = Av = 0 mod 3, so phi(p) = phi(q): collision. (b) If p != q in {0,1}^t with phi(p) = phi(q), then v = p - q in {-1,0,1}^t is nonzero and Av = 0 mod 3 (the constant c cancels), so rank A < t. Hence injective iff full column rank. label: S0053
statement: LEMMA (affine prefix fibres over F_p). Let p be prime, A in F_p^{k x t} with rank r, c in F_p^k, phi(x) = Ax + c, B = {0,1}^t, D_t = {a - b : a, b in B} inside F_p^t, K(A) = |ker A intersect D_t|. Then (i) every fibre F of phi satisfies |F intersect B| <= K(A) <= p^(t-r); (ii) phi is injective on B iff K(A) = 1; (iii) |phi(B)| >= 2^t / p^(t-r). label: S0091
statement: REPAIR LEMMA for S0038 (CLAIMED). Fix m, s; N = 2^m; Circ_s = circuits on m inputs, binary gates, size <= s; |Circ_s| <= (16 (m+s)^2)^s (m+s) = 2^{O(s log(m+s))}. I_s = {Eval(C) : C in Circ_s} subset {0,1}^N; f(x) = lex-first C in Circ_s with Eval(C) = x, for x in I_s. For a prefix p of length t and q in {0,1}^(N-t) set g_p(q) = f(pq) if pq in I_s, else bottom. CLAIM: (a) for every block b of length l, g_{pb}(q) = g_p(bq) (directly from the definition), so the map (g_p, b) -> g_{pb} is a well-defined transition table depending only on m, s; (b) P_t = {p : g_p not identically bottom} = prefixes of Eval(C) for C in Circ_s, and assigning to each p in P_t its lex-first witness is injective into Circ_s, so the number of distinct g_p is at most |P_t| + 1 <= |Circ_s| + 1; (c) at t = N, g_x(empty) = f(x), so the final state contains the search output. Hence a one-pass automaton computes search-MCSP^A[s] (any A; no oracle needed for the bound) with ceil(log2(|Circ_s|+1)) = O(s log(m+s)) bits of state, unbounded update time (the transition table is a finite function of (m,s)). PROOF: (a) by the definition of g. (b) if g_p is not bottom, some Eval(C) has prefix p, so p is in P_t; distinct g_p values can be attached to a common witness only through the injection above, and bottom is one value, giving the count. (c) by definition. SCOPE: state-count bound for search-MCSP^A with unbounded update time. Does not give a poly-time update and does not close G0004 or G0009.

label: S0095
statement: LEMMA A (fast path) and LEMMA B (monotone witness). Setting: Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs, totally ordered by a fixed injective encoding ord. N = 2^m. Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t, S(p) = {C : Eval(C) starts with p}, P_t = {p : S(p) nonempty}, and for p in P_t, w(p) = ord-least element of S(p). CLAIM A: if p in P_t, pb in P_{t+1}, and Eval(w(p))_{t+1} = b, then w(pb) = w(p). PROOF: w(p) has prefix pb, so w(p) is in S(pb). S(pb) is a subset of S(p), and w(p) is the least element of S(p), so it is also the least element of S(pb). QED. CLAIM B: if pb is in P_{t+1}, then w(p) <= w(pb). PROOF: S(pb) is a subset of S(p), so the minimum over S(p) is at most the minimum over S(pb). QED. COROLLARY: for a fixed Eval-string x, t -> w(x[:t]) is non-decreasing in ord. Scope: any total order on any circuit class; no complexity claim. CLASSIFICATION: Claim B and the corollary are bookkeeping, not progress. Claim A gives a per-step O(size(w(p))) fast path, but only when the bit matches.

structure.gap: OPEN (G0004 unchanged). (i) On a bit mismatch, w(pb) is the least element of S(pb) above w(p) in ord. Testing membership in S(pb) needs all t+1 bits of Eval(C), so no poly(s,m) per-step update is given. (ii) The number of slow-path events per stream is bounded only by |Circ_s| = 2^{O(s log(m+s))}, not by poly(s). Lemma A does not bound the mismatch frequency. Lemma B gives no poly bound on the number of witness changes.

label: S0098
statement: LINEAR-UPDATE DIMENSION LEMMA (restricted update class; closes nothing by itself, shrinks the linear case of G0004). Setting: F any field; N = 2^m; x in {0,1}^N; Im = Im_s = { truth tables of circuits of size <= s }; f = indicator of Im, valued in {0,1} inside F. A linear-update one-pass algorithm of dimension k over F: state s_0 in F^k fixed; s_t = A_{t,x_t} s_{t-1} for time-dependent matrices A_{t,b} in F^{k x k}; output c . s_N in F, required to equal f(x) for every x. (Affine updates are covered by adding one constant coordinate: dimension k+1.) Cut t: write x = p q with |p| = t, |q| = N - t. TRIANGULAR FOOLING SET at cut t: pairs (p_i, q_i), i = 1..r, with p_i q_i in Im for all i, and p_i q_j not in Im for all i > j (the cross entries with i < j are unconstrained). THEOREM: every such algorithm has k >= r. PROOF: for a prefix p let v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the product of the prefix transitions (depends only on p). For a suffix q let w_q = B_{t,q}^T c in F^k, where B_{t,q} is the product of the suffix transitions (depends only on q). Then f(pq) = c . B_{t,q} A_{t,p} s_0 = <w_q, v_p>. So the r x r matrix M[i,j] = f(p_i q_j) equals V^T W with V = [v_{p_1} ... v_{p_r}] and W = [w_{q_1} ... w_{q_r}] in F^{k x r}, hence rank_F M <= k. By the fooling conditions M[i,i] = 1 and M[i,j] = 0 for i > j, so M is upper unitriangular with det 1 and rank_F M = r. Hence k >= r. QED. SCOPE: linear updates over a field, any time-dependent matrices, any N, any cut, any field; it says nothing about general or nonlinear updates and nothing about update time beyond the dimension. Note: the trivial bound rank_F M_t(f) <= |Im| does NOT give a lower bound; only a triangular fooling set (or any rank lower bound) does. CONSEQUENCE: the linear-update case of G0004 (poly(s) dimension cannot decide or search MCSP[s]) reduces to exhibiting, for some cut, a triangular fooling set of size superpolynomial in s inside Im_s. OPEN (not claimed): whether such a set exists. A max-degree greedy argument does not give it, because the prefix degree of Im can be comparable to |Im| (e.g. all circuits whose first cofactor is 0). GAP: G0004 (restricted class only; general update time open); no claim about P vs NP.

By the fooling conditions M[i,i] = 1 and M[i,j] = 0 for i > j, so M is upper unitriangular with det 1 and rank_F M = r. Hence k >= r. QED. SCOPE: linear updates over a field, any time-dependent matrices, any N, any cut, any field; it says nothing about general or nonlinear updates and nothing about update time beyond the dimension. Note: the trivial bound rank_F M_t(f) <= |Im| does NOT give a lower bound; only a triangular fooling set (or any rank lower bound) does. CONSEQUENCE: the linear-update case of G0004 (poly(s) dimension cannot decide or search MCSP[s]) reduces to exhibiting, for some cut, a triangular fooling set of size superpolynomial in s inside Im_s. OPEN (not claimed): whether such a set exists. A max-degree greedy argument does not give it, because the prefix degree of Im can be comparable to |Im| (e.g. all circuits whose first cofactor is 0). GAP: G0004 (restricted class only; general update time open); no claim about P vs NP.

label: S0102
statement: CAP LEMMA (cut-rank cap). Let S be any set of N-bit truth tables, N=2^m. (a) For every 1<=t<N and every field F, rank_F M_t(S) <= |S|, where M_t[p][q]=1[(q<<t)|p in S]. Proof: each f in S sets exactly one entry of M_t, so M_t has at most |S| nonzero entries, hence at most |S| nonzero rows, and rank <= number of nonzero rows. (b) For S=Im_s, |Im_s| <= (16(m+s)^2)^s, since a size-<=s circuit is a sequence of at most s gates, each choosing an op (16) and two earlier nodes (at most (m+i)^2 choices for gate i). (c) For the prefix Myhill-Nerode classes of S at level t: the residual of prefix p is zero unless p is a prefix of some element of S, and distinct nonzero residuals need distinct prefixes, so the number of classes is at most |S|+1. Hence the minimal exact prefix automaton of Im_s has at most |Im_s|+1 states per level, i.e. O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the budget O(log N + s log(n+s)). Consequence: a cut-rank lower bound on the STATE count of this automaton cannot exceed O(s log(m+s)) bits. The S0098 route (k >= rank_F) therefore bounds only LINEAR-dimension models; it cannot establish a streaming lower bound beyond the budget, consistent with the protocol's statement that only an update-time lower bound can.

label: S0103
statement: REPAIR LEMMA (residual-function automaton for EXT prefix language). Let N = 2^m, s <= poly(m). For a prefix p of length t <= N, define the residual language R_p = { q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in Im_s } where Im_s is the set of truth tables of fan-in-2 circuits of size <= s over m inputs. (a) The number of distinct residual languages is at most |Im_s| + 1 <= (16(m+s)^2)^s + 1. Proof: distinct nonempty residuals correspond to distinct nonempty subsets of Im_s sharing the same prefix p, so there are at most |Im_s| of them; the empty residual (p not a prefix of any element of Im_s) adds at most one. (b) The minimal exact prefix automaton of the language Im_s therefore has at most |Im_s| + 1 states per level t, and total states at most (N+1)(|Im_s|+1). State bits per level: log2(|Im_s|+1) <= s log2(16(m+s)^2) + 1 = O(s log(m+s)). (c) The state transition function (update) given a new bit b: from state representing residual R, go to the state representing R.b = { q' : b q' in R }. Computing this update may require time exponential in s (unbounded update time), because testing whether a string q' is in R.b means checking whether p b q' in Im_s, i.e., whether a given truth table prefix extends to a circuit of size <= s. No poly(s) time update is claimed. (d) This automaton is exactly the Myhill-Nerode DFA of the language Im_s, and its state count at level t equals the number of Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes of prefixes of length t. The earlier claim r_t = |P_t| + [P_t != {0,1}^t] is corrected to r_t <= |P_t| + 1 where P_t is the set of length-t prefixes of Im_s, and the inequality can be strict because distinct prefixes may yield the same residual. (e) Consequence: any streaming algorithm that decides membership in Im_s must use at least log2(|Im_s|+1) bits of state, but this lower bound is only O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the O(log N + s log(n+s)) budget of the MMW19 Thm 1.2 algorithm. Hence a state-count lower bound alone cannot separate the EXT automaton from the budget. To obtain a separation, an UPDATE-TIME lower bound is needed, consistent with G0004.

This repair gives the correct state-count bound with unbounded update time, and fixes the exact-count formula.

label: S0108
statement: REPAIR of S0038 (state count only, no update-time claim). Setting: Im_s = set of truth tables of all nodes (inputs and gates) of circuits of size <= s over m inputs, N = 2^m. For t in 0..N, M_t = 2^t - 1, P_t = {f & M_t : f in Im_s}, and for p in {0,1}^t the residual R_p = {f >> t : f in Im_s, f & M_t = p}. CLAIM A: the number D_t of distinct residual sets satisfies D_t <= |P_t| + 1 <= |Im_s| + 1. PROOF: R_p is empty when p is not in P_t, so each nonempty residual set is R_p for some p in P_t, and the empty set adds at most one class. CLAIM B: |Im_s| <= 3(4(m+s)^2)^s. PROOF: at step k (0 <= k < s) a circuit has L_k <= m+s nodes, and the number of candidate new gates is at most L_k (negations) + 3 L_k^2 (ordered and, or, xor) <= a := 4(m+s)^2. Gate-creating choice sequences of length <= s number at most sum_{k=1}^{s} a^k <= 2a^s (a >= 2). Adding the m inputs gives |Im_s| <= m + 2a^s <= 3a^s. COROLLARY: D_t <= 3(4(m+s)^2)^s + 1, so log D_t = O(s log(m+s)) bits. SCOPE: state count of the prefix automaton of EXT_{m,s}; no update-time bound, so G0003 and G0004 remain open. The earlier constant 5(m+s)^2 is superseded by Claim B.

label: S0111
statement: Lemma L1 (bit-level residual transition). Proof: the level-(t+1) residual of an extended prefix is obtained by restricting the level-t residual to the assignments whose next bit equals b and then dropping that bit (shift by one). Restriction to bit value b selects exactly g in R_p with g&1 = b, and the shift g>>1 re-indexes the remaining bits. This is a direct unfolding of the residual definition, not a counting argument. Computational check: cm-2b9d70b2910543ec, exhaustive for (m,s) in {(2,1),(2,2),(3,1),(3,2)} and n_fails = 0 on all cases, plus m=4, s=1 with 131070 checks and n_fails = 0.

structure.gap: Scope is the bit-indexed residual definition as stated in the lemma; the unfolding is argued in words and has been checked on small cases only. It does not give an update-time bound and does not close G0003 or G0004. Next step: use L1 to bound the per-step update cost of the streaming system that tracks live and dead prefixes.

label: S0115
statement: PROOF: (i) If R_t(p) is nonempty, then p is a prefix of some tt in Im, so the map p -> R_t(p) is defined on at most |P_t| <= |Im| = L nonempty prefixes. (ii) Each distinct nonempty residual is the value of R_t at some nonempty prefix, so r_t <= |P_t| <= L. (iii) Adding the empty residual gives at most L+1 states per depth. (iv) L <= number of circuit encodings of size <= s, and each gate chooses two earlier nodes and a 4-bit op, so L <= (n+s+1)^{2s} 16^s, giving log L = O(s log(n+s)). The earlier claim 'r_t = |P_t| + [P_t != {0,1}^t]' is NOT used: distinct prefixes may share a residual, so only the upper bound is claimed.

label: S0121
statement: CLAIMED: LEMMA (cofactor transition). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, N=2^n, Im = {tt(C): C a circuit on n inputs of size <= s} subset {0,1}^N, M=|Im|. For a prefix p of length t and residual R_p = {q in {0,1}^(N-t) : pq in Im}, the following hold exactly. (i) For b in {0,1}: R_{pb} = {q' in {0,1}^(N-t-1) : bq' in R_p}, i.e. R_{pb} is the b-cofactor of R_p at its first coordinate. Proof: pbq' in Im iff bq' in R_p, by definition of R_p. (ii) R_{pb} is empty iff EXT_{n,s}(pb)=1 is false, where EXT_{n,s}(x)=1 iff some circuit of size <= s has truth table with prefix x. Proof: by definition. (iii) Hence the Myhill-Nerode classes of the prefix language of Im (read most-significant bit first) form a deterministic automaton whose state count is at most M+1 (the bound of G0062), and whose transition on bit b is the cofactor map on classes. Proof: (i) shows the transition is determined by R_p, and the state count is the G0062 bound.

structure.evidence: Argument-level, by definition. Not yet checked numerically. A finite check on n=3, s=1,2 would confirm that the number of distinct cofactor classes equals the G0062 count. It would test the transition identity (i) on explicit tables.
structure.gap: This is a REDUCTION, not a proof of a poly(s) update. Step (i) shows that the update needs only R_p itself, not the circuit family as such. But computing the class of the cofactor from the class of R_p requires comparing residual sets, which is a computation over the table of Im of size M <= (c(n+s)^2)^(s+1). That gives update time poly(M), not poly(s). G0003 and G0004 remain open. Open question: is there a poly(s)-time procedure for the cofactor-class map, or for EXT_{n,s} restricted to the prefix trie? Any such procedure would be a new ALGORITHM step.

label: S0125
statement: LEMMA (exponential-time update, not poly(s)). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, N=2^n, Im = {tt(C): C circuit on n inputs, size <= s}. For any prefix p of length t, EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff some C in Im has prefix p. PROOF: Every circuit of size <= s over binary fan-in gates is specified by at most s gates; gate k has an op from a set of 16 binary Boolean functions and two inputs among the n+k-1 earlier nodes, plus a choice of output node. So the number of circuits is at most (16 (n+s)^2)^(s+1). Each truth table has N bits and is computed in poly(N) * s time by evaluating gates on N-bit words. Enumerating all circuits and checking prefix p therefore decides EXT_{n,s}(p) in time (16 (n+s)^2)^(s+1) * poly(N). The update for bit b on state p is one such query, so the update time is 2^{O(s log(n+s))} * poly(2^n). SCOPE: a general upper bound, exponential in s. It does NOT bound update time by poly(s), so it does not close G0003 (which needs poly(s) update) and does not touch G0004 (a lower bound).

statement: LEMMA L1 (aligned-prefix restriction). For n>=1, s>=1, 0<=k<=n, with the first 2^k truth-table indices being the subcube x_{k+1..n}=0: {tt(C) mod 2^(2^k) : C an n-input circuit of size<=s} = Im_{k,s}. Proof: (subset) substitute 0 for x_{k+1..n}; gate count does not increase. (superset) a k-input circuit ignores extra inputs. Consequence: the EXT query at aligned length 2^k equals MCSP-membership on 2^k-bit tables, enumerable in N(log N)^{O(s)} time for fixed s. label: S0135
statement: LEMMA (amortized witness automaton, S0091/S0095 setting). Fix m, s, the total order ord on Circ_s, and a string x of length N=2^m. Let w_t = ord-least circuit C with Eval(C) starting with x[:t]. statement: LEMMA R (rank form of the linear-update bound; tightens S0098 from a triangular fooling set to the full cut rank). Setting: F a field, N = 2^m, Im = Im_s as in S0098, f = indicator of Im valued in F. A linear-update one-pass algorithm of dimension k over F computes f on {0,1}^N. Fix a cut t and let M_t be the 2^t x 2^(N-t) matrix M_t[p,q] = f(pq) over F. CLAIM: k >= rank_F(M_t) for every t. PROOF: the transitions A_{i,b} are fixed per position i, so for a prefix p of length t the state after reading p is v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the ordered product of the prefix transitions. For a suffix q of length N-t, the remaining transitions give s_N = B_q v_p with B_q in F^{k x k} depending only on q. The output is c . s_N, so f(pq) = u_q . v_p with u_q = c B_q in F^(1 x k). Hence M_t = U V where U has rows u_q (2^(N-t) x k) and V has columns v_p (k x 2^t), so rank_F M_t <= k. COROLLARY: k >= max_t rank_F M_t, which is at least the size of any triangular fooling set (the upper-triangular principal submatrix with unit diagonal has det 1). SCOPE: exact for linear-update algorithms over the field F; the bound is field-dependent in general: rank_Q and rank_{F_p} of an integer matrix can differ (rank_{F_p} <= rank_Q), so the bound for an F_p-algorithm must use rank over F_p. Does not give a poly-time or update-time bound, does not close G0004. Upper limit: rank_F M_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |Im_s|) with |Im_s| = 2^(O(s log(m+s))), so the rank bound cannot exceed the circuit-count bound of S0091 in magnitude.

label: S0144
statement: LEMMA L1 (fixed-s streaming for membership in Im_s; bookkeeping, not progress). Setting: m, s >= 1; Circ_s = straight-line programs of length k, 1 <= k <= s, where step j (j = 1..k) applies one of the 4 ops {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b} to a pair a < b of the m+j-1 earlier nodes. Im_s = truth tables of Circ_s. (i) COUNT: a program of length k is determined by its sequence of choices (op_j, a_j, b_j), and there are at most 4*C(m+j-1,2) <= 2(m+s)^2 choices at step j, so the number of programs of length k is at most (2(m+s)^2)^k, and |Circ_s| <= sum_{k=1..s} (2(m+s)^2)^k <= 2(2(m+s)^2)^s, since the ratio r = 2(m+s)^2 >= 2 makes the geometric sum at most 2 r^s. (ii) ALGORITHM: read x_1..x_N in order and keep the alive set A_t = {C in Circ_s : C(y) = x_y for all y <= t}, stored as a bit vector of length |Circ_s|. Start with A_0 = Circ_s. At step t, for each alive C, compute C(y_t) for the input y_t with binary expansion t in O(s+m) time, and drop C if it differs from x_t. Then A_N = {C : Eval(C) = x}, and the output is 1 iff A_N is nonempty. (iii) CORRECTNESS: by induction on t, A_t is exactly the consistent set, so the output decides x in Im_s exactly. (iv) COST: state |Circ_s| bits, per-bit time O(|Circ_s|(s+m)), so for fixed s both are poly(m) with degree O(s). For s = m^c the bound is 2^{Theta(s log m)}, superpolynomial. PROOF COMPLETE for (i)-(iv). SCOPE: membership in Im_s for fixed s only. Does NOT bound the update cost for s = poly(m), and does NOT close G0004 or G0071-G0074. Its state bound is the trivial one; the O(s log(m+s)) bit bound would need S0091, which is still unreviewed. NOT SELF-REVIEWABLE: author family equals this session's family, so it stays CLAIMED until another family reviews it.

label: S0145
statement: LEMMA (state count of the EXT prefix automaton, restricted class B, |B|=b). Let B be a finite binary basis (here AND, OR, XOR, so b=3; no negation or constants), let N=2^m, let C_{m,s} be the circuits of size <= s over inputs x_1..x_m with fan-in-2 gates from B, and let Im_{m,s} subset {0,1}^N be their truth tables. Then (a) |Im_{m,s}| <= prod_{k=0}^{s-1} b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 <= (b(m+s)^2)^s. (b) For every t in 0..N and every prefix p in {0,1}^t, let R_t(p) = {w in {0,1}^{N-t} : pw in Im}. The number of distinct nonempty R_t(p) is at most |Im_{m,s}|. Hence the minimal (Myhill-Nerode) automaton reading the truth table has at most |Im_{m,s}| states at each level, i.e. log(#states) = O(s log(m+s)) bits, plus log N bits for the position counter. PROOF (a): a circuit of size s is determined by the sequence of gates; gate k picks an unordered pair {i<=j} from the m+k available nodes and one of b operations, giving at most b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 choices; the map from sequences to truth tables is onto Im, so |Im| is at most the product. PROOF (b): restriction to the first t bits maps Im onto the set of realised prefixes, so #realised prefixes <= |Im|; R_t(p) depends only on p, so the number of distinct residuals is at most the number of realised prefixes. Both steps are elementary counting.

statement: PROOF. (1) rank_F M <= |S|: rank is at most the number of nonzero rows; each nonzero row holds at least one 1; the map x -> (x>>(N-t), x mod 2^(N-t)) is injective and each x in S sets exactly one entry, so the number of 1-entries is |S|. Hence rank_F M_t(S) <= |S| for every field F. (2) |Im_s| bound: every function in Im_s is the value of some gate of a program with j <= s gates (or a base node). A program of j gates is a sequence where gate k (1<=k<=j) is op_c(a,b) with c in [16] and a,b among the m+2+(k-1) = m+1+k earlier nodes. So the number of programs with j gates is at most prod_{k=1}^{j} 16(m+1+k)^2 <= (16(m+s+1)^2)^j, because m+1+k <= m+s+1 for k <= s. The base nodes contribute at most m+2 <= 16(m+s+1)^2 values. Summing over j=0..s: |Im_s| <= sum_{j=0}^{s} (16(m+s+1)^2)^j <= (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s. Combining (1) and (2) gives the lemma. Consistency check (not a proof step): m=3, s=2 gives |Im_2|=152 <= 3*(16*36)^2; m=4, s=2 gives |Im_2|=526 <= 3*(16*49)^2.

statement: LEMMA (F_2 affine images: streaming membership). Let r, L >= 1, M_1..M_L in F_2^r (row vectors), c in F_2^L, and phi(z)_t = <M_t, z> + c_t for z in F_2^r. Let Im = phi(F_2^r). For a prefix p of length t, p is a prefix of some element of Im iff the linear system {<M_s, z> = p_s + c_s : s <= t} is consistent over F_2. Maintain the reduced row-echelon basis of the augmented system (rows (M_s | p_s + c_s)), with at most r pivots. Appending bit b to p is one insertion: reduce the new augmented row by the existing pivot rows (at most r XORs of (r+1)-bit words), declare p dead iff the reduced row is 0 with rhs 1, otherwise add it as a new pivot and clear its pivot column from the other rows. Correctness: the system is consistent iff no F_2-combination of its rows gives 0 = 1; the reduced echelon basis spans exactly the row space of the augmented system, so it detects inconsistency. Consequences: (i) x in {0,1}^L lies in Im iff the full system with rhs x_s + c_s is consistent, decidable in one pass with state O(r^2) bits and update time O(r^2) word operations per bit, with no exponential branching needed; (ii) the trie of Im restricted to affine images is poly-state per prefix. SCOPE: F_2 affine images only, z over all of F_2^r (no circuit, no size bound s). It does NOT address G0004, which concerns Im(Eval) of circuits of size <= s, where the extension question is an existential over Circ_s. This is standard Gaussian elimination, recorded as a restricted-class special case; it is bookkeeping and does not count as progress toward P vs NP. Verification: cm-697a9a9912a04eca (own code, 400 random F_2 affine instances, r<=5, L<=9, full brute-force prefix sets, 0 violations)

statement: L-FR (field-robust fooling bound, restates S0098 with the field explicit). Let M be a 0/1 matrix indexed by P x Q and F any field. If rows p_1..p_r and columns q_1..q_r satisfy M[p_i,q_j]=0 for i>j and M[p_i,q_i]=1, then rank_F(M) >= r for EVERY field F. Proof: the r x r submatrix is upper-triangular with unit diagonal, so its determinant is 1 in F. Corollary: for any prime p, rank_p(M) <= rank_Q(M) for integer M (a nonzero r x r minor mod p is nonzero over Z), so the rational rank bounds each GF(p) rank from above. Scope: a lower bound on any field's cut rank; no update-time bound; does NOT close or shrink G0004.

label: S0171
statement: SIZE-1 STREAMING LEMMA (special case s=1; does NOT close G0004 or G0009). Setting: N=2^m, x in {0,1}^N, Im_1 = truth tables of circuits of size <= 1 on m inputs over binary gates {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b}, plus constants and literals. Cand_m = the deduplicated list of truth tables of {0, 1, x_i (i<m), op(x_i,x_j) (i!=j, op in the four ops)}; |Cand_m| <= 4m(m-1)+m+2 = O(m^2). Filter: alive_0 = Cand_m; on reading bit b_t, alive_{t+1} = {c in alive_t : c[t] = b_t}. CLAIM: after N bits, alive_N = {c in Cand_m : c = x} = Cand_m cap {x}, so x in Im_1 iff alive_N is nonempty. PROOF: induction on t, alive_t = {c : c agrees with x on positions < t}; at t=N the agreement is equality. Per-bit update costs O(|alive_t|) <= O(m^2) = O(log^2 N) comparisons; state is one bit per candidate, O(m^2) bits. SCOPE: size <= 1 only. Its per-bit cost is poly(log N) only because |Im_1| is polynomial; for general s, |Circ_s| = 2^{Theta(s log(m+s))}, so this filter is superpolynomial in m when s = poly(m).
